title: Theoretical Insights into Fine-Tuning Attention Mechanism: Generalization and Optimization

contributions.purpose: Explain theoretically the 'Unequal Importance of Attention Matrices' phenomenon and justify why fine-tuning only Wq and Wv is preferable to fine-tuning all three (Wq, Wk, Wv).
contributions.mechanism: Information-theoretic generalization analysis: establish generalization bounds (Theorem 1) for fine-tuning pre-trained attention models, showing fine-tuning Wq,Wv reduces parameters while improving the generalization bound. Motivated by the observation that as weights approach zero the gradients of Wq,Wk vanish while Wv's gradient stays non-zero due to softmax normalization.
contributions.evaluation: Theorem 1 generalization bound (theoretical). Empirically, optimizing Wv yields significantly better performance than optimizing Wk; fine-tuning only Wq and Wv is comparable to or better than all three matrices while cutting tunable parameters by ~1/3.
contributions.domain: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of LLMs / attention mechanism theory
contributions.source_quote: Generalization: advantages of fine-tuning Wq, Wv over Wq, Wk, Wv together. We perform a thorough theoretical analysis to demonstrate the advantages. To be more specific, we employ information-theoretic approaches to establish the generalization bounds of fine-tuning pre-trained models with attention mechanism (See Theorem 1 for details). This indicates that fine-tuning Wq, Wv instead of Wq, Wk, Wv reduces the number of parameters, while improving generalization bounds and potentially providing memory benefits.

contributions.purpose: Explain the 'Attention Matrices with Customized Learning Rate Leads to Better Convergence' phenomenon and justify assigning a higher learning rate to Wv.
contributions.mechanism: Convergence/optimization analysis of the attention mechanism: analyze learning dynamics (Case 1, showing Wv may learn inefficiently) and use scaling arguments for large-width networks to derive Theorem 2, showing efficient feature learning requires the Wv learning rate to be much larger than that of Wq, Wk.
contributions.evaluation: Theorem 2 (theoretical) on efficient feature learning under large-width scaling. A higher learning rate for Wv relative to Wq/Wk accelerates convergence and improves performance.
contributions.domain: Optimization / learning-rate tuning for attention fine-tuning
contributions.source_quote: Optimization: convergence analysis of attention mechanism with varying learning rate settings. ... by using scaling arguments for large width-n networks we illustrate (Theorem 2) that the feature learning of attention mechanism is efficient when the learning rate for Wv should be generally much larger than that of Wq, Wk in fine-tuning.

contributions.purpose: Turn the theoretical insights into a practical fine-tuning strategy that improves storage and time efficiency.
contributions.mechanism: A new fine-tuning strategy that fine-tunes Wq, Wv with customized (higher for Wv) learning rates, derived from the two theoretical insights.
contributions.evaluation: Experiments on benchmark datasets and open-source pre-trained models verify the strategy visibly improves fine-tuning efficiency. Authors explicitly do NOT compare against other PEFT methods, positioning the strategy only as a demonstration that theory can guide practice.
contributions.source_quote: Building on our experimental and theoretical insights, one can develop new algorithms to improve the effectiveness (e.g., storage, and time) of fine-tuning. Experimental results for our strategy (in Section 5) on benchmark datasets and open source pre-trained models verify that the method can visibly influence fine-tuning efficiency.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Some studies treat Wq and Wk as a single unit (Wqk = Wq Wk^T), however, the benefits of fine-tuning Wq, Wv alone have yet to be further clarified.

While certain empirical guidelines, such as the original Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), explore which weight matrices in transformers are suitable for the application of LoRA, comprehensive theoretical analyses of these phenomena are still limited.

A unified framework for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Building on the work of [16], we consider a unified framework that establishes connections among various parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods.

notes: Primarily a theory paper providing generalization (Theorem 1) and optimization (Theorem 2) analyses to explain two empirical attention fine-tuning phenomena, plus a derived strategy. Important caveat/limitation the authors state themselves: they deliberately do NOT compare against existing PEFT methods, so the strategy's competitiveness vs LoRA etc. is not established -- experiments only aim to validate the theory. No negative result reported, but the scope of empirical validation is intentionally narrow.
